text:
I stood on the Tessaly Fjord viewing platform on 14 March 2031 as the tidal plant finished its final commissioning test, and the number the engineers had been waiting for came up on the control room screen: 95 megawatts.

Dr. Ingrid Halvorsen-Pell, chief engineer of the Tessaly Fjord Energy Authority, signed off on the rating once the test closed. Staff told me the figure rests on the plant's 12 turbines, each contributing roughly 7.9 megawatts, which together give the combined rated capacity.

The Authority published the result in the Tessaly Fjord Commissioning Report (Ref. TFEA-CR-2031/07) at the end of the test. I read the report's rating section and it matches what I saw on the screen and what staff told me on site.

The plant is now rated at 95 megawatts. Anyone wanting to check the detail can request the report from the Authority using the reference above.
